medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive in metabolic syndrome
NICE NG136 recommends CCB in combination with ACE‑I for hypertension

medications.dose: 20 mg oral tablet in the evening
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 advises a statin for anyone with QRISK ≥10 % or metabolic‑syndrome components

medications.dose: 500 mg once daily with evening meal, titrate after 1 week to 500 mg twice daily, then to 1000 mg twice daily as tolerated (max 2 g/day)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin as first‑line oral therapy for high‑risk pre‑diabetes when lifestyle alone is insufficient

medications.dose: 120 mg three times daily with each main meal containing fat (≤30 g per meal)
medications.purpose: Obesity weight management adjunct to lifestyle
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 lists Orlistat as the licensed oral anti‑obesity drug for BMI ≥30 kg/m² (or ≥28 with comorbidities)

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase plasma concentrations of atorvastatin (CYP3A4 inhibition), raising risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis.
interactions_checked.action: Use low‑dose atorvastatin (20 mg) and monitor CK if muscle symptoms develop.

contraindications.reason: Contra‑indicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (risk of lactic acidosis). Patient eGFR not available.
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR <30, omit metformin and consider GLP‑1 RA for weight and glycaemic control.

contraindications.reason: Avoided because urine microscopy shows leukocytes (possible UTI) and NICE NG28 lists recurrent UTI as a contraindication.
contraindications.alternative: Treat any urinary infection first; consider SGLT2i only after infection cleared and if renal function permits.

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥45 mL/min/1.73 m² for metformin initiation; must obtain serum creatinine/eGFR before starting.
Baseline liver function tests not available – required before initiating atorvastatin.
Fasting lipid profile and QRISK score missing – needed to confirm statin indication and to document cardiovascular risk.
Urine culture not performed – urine leukocytes suggest possible infection; must treat before any SGLT2i consideration.
Allergy history not documented – verify no hypersensitivity to ACE‑I, statin, metformin, or orlistat.
treatment_summary: Continue the ACE‑I/CCB regimen for hypertension (already at target). Initiate atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for cardiovascular risk reduction, start metformin XR with titration for prediabetes (pending eGFR), and add orlistat 120 mg TID for obesity management. Monitor renal function, liver enzymes, CK, and treat any urinary infection before considering SGLT2 inhibitors. Review all results in 2 weeks, then schedule annual medication reviews per NICE guidance.
